source.title: The USSR Olympiad Problem Book: Selected Problems and Theorems of Elementary Mathematics

accepted.question_text: In the counterfeit-coin weighing problem, there are 1000 similar coins and exactly one is counterfeit. The counterfeit coin has a different weight from a genuine coin, but it is not known in advance whether it is lighter or heavier. Using a pan balance, what is the minimum number of weighings needed to locate the counterfeit coin when the procedure is not required to determine whether the counterfeit is light or heavy?

evidence.quote: There is one counterfeit coin among 1000 similar coins.
if we are relieved of the necessity of determining whether it is light or heavy.

trace.notes: Normalized one URL input as a zbMATH resolver record: https://zbmath.org/3273098.

Direct fetch of the zbMATH page returned a Cloudflare challenge. The zbMATH REST API record 3273098 identified the work as Shklarsky, Chentzov, and Yaglom, The USSR olympiad problem book. Selected problems and theorems of elementary mathematics, W.H. Freeman, 1962. A readable HTML copy was accepted because its visible title, authors, translator/editor, and bibliographical note state that the Dover edition is an unabridged and unaltered republication of the work first published by W.H. Freeman and Company, San Francisco, in 1962.

Mapped the HTML source. Front matter appears at lines 32-355. The contents list identifies twelve problem sections and separate solution and hint sections at lines 249-262. The source is a solved olympiad problem book rather than a research open-problem paper; likely question regions are numbered problem statements in sections 1-12.

In section 1, Introductory Problems, extracted the explicit open-ended remark following Problem 6(b): the source asks for the least number of weighings when locating the counterfeit coin but not determining whether it is light or heavy.

Searched the readable HTML for explicit open-problem markers including 'would be interesting', 'open', 'unsolved', and 'unknown'. Only the Problem 6 remark matched as an open-ended candidate; other numbered problems are ordinary solved olympiad exercises with solutions and hints.

Rewrote the remark into a standalone question by inlining the 1000-coin setting, the unknown lighter-or-heavier condition, the pan-balance method, and the relaxed objective of locating the counterfeit without identifying its direction of weight difference.
No near-duplicate open-ended candidate was found.

Accepted. The rewritten question is self-contained, evidence-backed by stable HTML line locators, and does not introduce unsupported facts. is_solved is false because the chosen source asks the variant as an interesting determination problem and does not explicitly mark it solved in that form.
Saved exact JSON output to outputs/parse-paper/3273098.json and outputs/latest.json.
